loan_project_research.question: Who authored the 'Loan' project visible in the capture: title 'Loan - Microsoft Visual Basic [design]', LOAN.FRM, form LoanSheet, controls grdPayments (Grid) and cmdCalcAmort, menus Options / Down Payment / Loan Length, frames 'Years in Loan' and 'Interest Rates', buttons 'Show Payments...' and 'Show Amortization...'?
loan_project_research.hypothesis_tested: A sample application Microsoft shipped with Visual Basic 4.0 (for example in the VB4 SAMPLES directory, perhaps a Grid control demo).
loan_project_research.conclusion: Microsoft sample (evidence: Microsoft KB Q150726 lists loan.frm, loan.frx and loan.vbp in \vb\samples\grid among the files installed by the Samples option in all editions of Visual Basic 4.0; three archive.org Visual Basic 4.0 CD contents listings (Enterprise 1995, Enterprise 1996, Professional 4.0a) each show VB/SAMPLES/GRID/LOAN.FRM 31,035 bytes, LOAN.FRX 2,336 bytes and LOAN.VBP 382 bytes; the capture shows a project named 'Loan' whose form file is LOAN.FRM and whose selected control is a Grid, which is what the \vb\samples\grid sample directory contains).
loan_project_research.confidence_and_limit: High for 'Loan / LOAN.FRM is the Microsoft VB 4.0 Grid sample'. The form's contents (LoanSheet, grdPayments, cmdCalcAmort, menus) were not compared with the text of LOAN.FRM, because reading it would mean extracting a file from a disc image; that was not done. The identification rests on the project name, the form file name, the Grid control, and the Samples listing, with no competing 'Loan' project found in any source searched.
loan_project_research.effect: No third-party content concern remains for the 'Loan' project: it is Microsoft content, the same rights holder as the IDE. This does not clear release. Whether Microsoft's screenshot permission (or another basis) covers the capture is still RQ-HIST-02-1, and XTRA-05 R14 stays blocked on it. RQ-HIST-02-2 in HIST-02 is answered by this evidence; the HIST-02 record itself was not edited (read-only for this worker).
loan_project_research.method: Read-only web lookups on 2026-09-15 with a generic browser User-Agent (no personal identifiers in headers); no accounts, no terms accepted, no borrow-gated books. Only HTML listing pages and KB article pages were fetched, into the worker scratchpad; no installer, disc image or file from inside a disc image was downloaded, and nothing third-party was added to the repository. URLs, quotes and SHA-256 hashes of the fetched pages are recorded here.

review_questions.question: The narration over this visual (War/SCRIPT.md:135) says the form was 'in the center' as 'a blank gray window' and the code window was 'behind all of it'. In the only accepted VB4 capture the form is centre-left, it is a populated Microsoft sample (LoanSheet), and the Code window is open in front of the form. Toolbox-left and properties-right match. Keep the narration as a general description of the IDE (possibly with 'behind' read as 'the code behind the form'), soften it (for example 'and a code window where you wrote your actual BASIC'), or ask the edit to hold on the clean screenshot during that sentence? No script edit was made and the art is unchanged.

No credit is burned into any variant, because HIST-02's proposed credit ('... Used with permission from Microsoft.') must not be used before the rights basis is decided. If Microsoft's screenshot permission is the chosen basis, where should the required statement go: video description, end credits, or on screen? Layout facts for the decision (no art changed): side-by-side leaves an empty dark area below the clean screenshot inside the safe area (about x 120-935, y 770-1008), so an on-screen line would fit there without re-layout; five-callouts and clean-workspace at 1.5x have no room inside the safe area below the screenshot (an on-screen line would need the image reduced to about 1.44x and a re-render).
Who authored the 'Loan' project (LOAN.FRM, form LoanSheet) shown whole in every variant?

resolution.limit: Form file text not compared (no disc-image extraction).
